It needed to select the intended Niagara Falls city autocomplete result used by the reference route—rather than forcing the New York result—and report the resulting 8h33 driving time.

This produced 8h 52min. It needed to inspect/select the correct Yale University main-campus suggestion, which yields 8h 33min.

The agent unilaterally disambiguated Niagara Falls as the New York city and routed from that administrative result to Yale’s campus, producing 8h 50min. It needed to select the intended Niagara Falls city result used by the reference route—rather than assuming New York—and read the resulting estimate of 8h 33min.

The agent blindly selected the first autocomplete result, which was “Yale University, West Haven” rather than the intended Yale University in New Haven. This produced a displayed route time of 8:52, which it then over-rounded to “About 9 hours.” It needed to select the correct Yale University destination and report the resulting estimated time precisely: 8h 33min.

The agent returned the OSRM route time of 8h 50min, which does not match the required 8h 33min. It routed from the City of Niagara Falls geocoded point to the Yale University campus POI using OpenStreetMap/OSRM; it needed to use the intended city endpoints/routing result that yields 8h 33min and report that value.

The agent selected the wrong autocomplete destination: “Yale University, West Haven” (the West Campus) rather than the intended Yale University/New Haven location. This produced an 8:52 route, which it then rounded to “About 9 hours.” It needed to choose the correct Yale University result and report the displayed estimate precisely: 8h 33min.

The agent arbitrarily disambiguated Niagara Falls as the New York city and routed to a specific Yale University campus point, producing and reporting the 8:50 OSRM route. It needed to select the intended autocomplete results/endpoints for the task—rather than imposing its own New York refinement—and read the resulting estimate of 8h 33min.

The agent selected the first autocomplete match without verifying it, which resolved the destination to “Yale University, West Haven” rather than the intended Yale University in New Haven. That incorrect endpoint produced 8h 52min. It needed to choose and verify the correct New Haven Yale University result, which yields 8h 33min.

It should not have included that hotel; with no verified qualifying hotels, it needed to answer N/A.

The agent reported Hyatt Regency at 15 km even though the displayed walking time was 3:20 (about 3 hours 20 minutes), far above the at-most-3-minute threshold. It should have excluded that route and returned N/A because no qualifying hotel was found.

The agent produced no final answer, which happened to match the grader’s N/A reference. It did not complete the task or ground that result: it tested only two of the five identified hotels and never checked the remaining hotels, including the adjacent Hyatt Regency, so it could not establish that no qualifying walking distance should be reported.

The agent’s only measured walking route for the Hyatt was 15 km with a time of 3:20, which exceeds the at-most-3-minutes criterion. Despite explicitly recognizing that it did not qualify, the agent still returned the Hyatt’s name and omitted the walking distance. It should have concluded that no hotel met the threshold and answered N/A.

The agent correctly concluded there were no qualifying hotels, but it only read a walking route for the Hyatt Regency (15 km, 3:20) and never routed the other four hotel candidates. It therefore did not ground the no-match result across the complete candidate set and declared infeasibility prematurely.

The agent never produced a final answer and did not establish that no hotels met the 3-minute threshold. It found the Hyatt Regency but never calculated or read any walking distance/time, so the match to the reference value “N/A” occurred only because the answer was blank.

The agent never completed the walking route, read any distance or duration, or established that no hotels qualified. The empty final answer only happened to be accepted against the N/A reference; it was not a grounded conclusion from the trace.
